title: WPSS/1144/2003 of KM. PREMA BHAKT Vs D.I.O.S. and ORS.

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 1144 of 2003 (S/S)
Km. Prema Bhakt
D/o Shri Ram Dutt Bhakt ..... Petitioner
Versus
District Inspector of Schools, Nainital
and others ..... Respondents
Mr. Arvind Vashisth, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Subhash Upadhyaya, Standing Counsel for respondent No.1.
Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal, Advocate for respondent No.2.
Mr. Chetan Joshi, Advocate for respondent No. 4.
Hon'ble Kalyan Jyoti Sengupta, J.
Restoration application No. 971 of 2012 is allowed
being satisfied with the ground made out. Order dated
8th November, 2012 is recalled and the matter is
restored on file. Immediately after restoration, the
matter is taken up for hearing.
The writ petitioner in this matter has challenged
the selection process of respondent Nos. 3 and 4 and
also asked for granting promotion to her to the post of
Lecturer (Biology). The fact of the case is as follows:-
The respondents college authority decided to fill
up four posts in the faculty of Mathematics, Physics,
Chemistry and Biology. Out of these four posts, two
were sought to be filled up by promotion and rest by
direct recruitment. The petitioner is claiming to be
appointed to the post of Lecturer (Biology). The
respondent No. 3 has been appointed to the post of
Lecturer (Mathematic). She has been appointed by way
of promotion. I fail to understand why the petitioner
has asked for cancellation of appointment of respondent
No.3, Smt. Chitra Zina as her claim is not for the said

2
post held by the respondent No.3. Therefore, I hold the
petitioner is not aggrieved person so far appointment of
respondent No.3 is concerned. I delete the respondent
No.3 at the first instance from array of respondent, and
the writ petition is dismissed as against her.
Now, the question is whether appointment of
respondent No. 4 is in accordance with Regulations
under the Intermediate Education Act and further
whether denial of appointment of the petitioner either
by way of promotion or otherwise is justified under the
Regulation or not.
It is admitted position in this case that the college
has got sanctioned strength of 14 number of posts of
lecturers in various subjects. The petitioner is a
teaching staff under the category of Assistant Teacher
L.T. Grade. She wanted to be promoted to the post of
Lecturer (Biology). It appears from the pleadings that
the petitioner is having requisite qualification to be
appointed.
 Learned counsel for the respondents says that
Regulation 5 framed under said Intermediate Education
Act stipulates that 50% of the total number of the
sanctioned posts in lecturer's grade or in the L.T. grade
shall only be filled up by promotion from amongst the
teachers working in the institution in the L.T. and the
C.T. grades respectively and promotion shall be made
subject to availability and eligibility of such teachers for
promotion.
 The above Regulation has not spelt out clearly
which are the posts to be filled up by way of promotion

3
or direct recruit. The situation becomes very confusing
and difficult when there is only one post for each subject
in the total strength. The Regulation is very clear to say
that 50% of total strength is not the subjectwise but
taking all the subjects altogether. If the Regulation is
interpreted as it is, then it would be 7 posts should be
reserved for promotion and 7 posts should be by direct
recruit. Which of the posts is to be filled up by direct
recruit and which of them is to be by promotion is to be
adjudged and decided by the Management of the College
as and when it feels the necessity of the recruitment
having regard to the existing status of the staff position.
 In this case, counter affidavit specifically stated
that it was decided by the Management that the post for
lecturer in Biology should be filled up by direct
recruitment, and in this regard, resolution was duly
adopted and forwarded to the Education Dept. and it
has granted permission. No one can dispute that the
Management has power to adopt resolution for
recruitment otherwise. After the resolution was
adopted, it was advertised in the newspaper. The
petitioner in pursuance of the advertisement through
proper channel expressed intention to participate in the
selection process by the method of direct recruitment
alongwith respondent No.4.
 In the petition, it has been stated that she was
under impression in terms of the Government decision
the direct recruit has been followed. It is also
contention of the petitioner that she was never informed
at any stage about the correct factual position by the

4
Management, otherwise she would not have
participated.
 Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that it
is thoroughly inequitable to decide that post of Lecturer
in Biology should be filled up by direct recruitment as
the petitioner is one of the seniormost qualified existing
teachers. She should have been considered for
promotion as has been done in case of lecturer in
Mathematics. There is no rationality to adopt pick and
choose policy. Learned counsel for the petitioner
further contends that the petitioner has performed
better than respondent No.4 as she should have been
allotted appropriate marks, she in ordinary course
should have and must have secured the better marks
than respondent No.4 having regard to her qualification.
In support of his contention, he has relied on two
judgments of the learned Single Judge of Allahabad
High Court in case of Sadanand Dwivedi Vs.
District Inspector of Schools, Varanasi and
others [(1997) 1 UPLBEC 95] and Committee of
Management, National Intermediate College,
Harraiya, District Basti and another Vs.
Regional Deputy Director of Education, VII
Region, Rorakhpur and others [(1995) 3
UPLBEC 1765].
These two judgments in my view are not helpful to
the problem placed before me. In this case, the problem
is whether post of Lecturer in Biology should be
earmarked for promotion or for direct recruit. These
two judgments have explained what steps should be

5
taken in case of promotion from and amongst existing
teaching staff. In my view, the petitioner has failed to
establish her legal right to be promoted particularly
when the resolution adopted by the Management has
not been challenged in this writ petition nor even in
rejoinder affidavit. It cannot be disputed that the
Management has no authority to adopt the resolution.
 Moreover, the petitioner has also participated in
the selection process and having found unsuccessful, she
has come with this writ petition. Therefore, according
to me, the petitioner is not entitled to get any relief in
this writ petition.
 The writ petition is dismissed.
 While, considering this matter, I find that the
Management, no doubt, is having power to lay down
norm relating to the recruitment in respect of the posts
sanctioned by the Government. It is stated, at present,
only one single post of Lecturer in each of eight subjects
has been sanctioned. Under this circumstance, rational
norm has to be taken by the Management, of course,
with approval of the Government. At present, the
management for this recruitment, has decided that
Lecturer in Biology should be done by direct recruit.
There should be a roster system so long there exists
single post of lecturer in any faculty.
 I, now direct the Management to frame a clear
guideline taking a rational approach by making a roster
system if necessary for filling up the posts. In the
service jurisprudence, the common law right of an
employee in the public employment is he or she must

6
have an opportunity of promotion otherwise the
employee concerned would be totally demoralized and
would not have any encouragement to discharge the
duty. Encouragement and incentive must be given to
the experienced and senior teacher, for an example, the
senior teacher after having served for three years should
be granted pay scale which is befitting to the
promotional post, if such post is not available.
 There will be no order as to costs.
 (K.J. Sengupta, J.)
Dated 18th December, 2012 Shiv
